note:
P1-91, filed 2026-08-13 by P1-90's live validation. FIRST ticket on the js-ninjatrader-mcp profile, and the first agent-loop ticket in this repo at all. The profile exists because tvDownloadOHLC's python-tvdownloadohlc cannot gate a .js file: its build_cmd is py_compile and its test_cmd is two Python suites that pass whatever a patch does here.

The acceptance tests were written BY HAND FIRST and are RED at the 36/39 baseline. tests/*.test.js is a PROTECTED path -- the implementer cannot reach them and must not try. Three fail now and must pass; three others in the same file already pass and must STAY passing, one of which exists specifically to stop this fix being over-applied.

BACKGROUND YOU NEED. P1-90 (closed, deployed, live-validated) made the NT8 addon REFUSE an account it cannot resolve, instead of falling back to the account named "Sim101", then to any non-Backtest account, then to any account at all -- and placing the order there. The addon is fixed. This ticket is the wrapper still advertising the guess the addon stopped honouring.

WHY A `default:` IS NOT DOCUMENTATION. An MCP client is permitted to materialise a schema default into the request. A client that does would inject a real, connected account name into an ORDER call; the addon would resolve it happily and the refusal would never be reached -- P1-90 re-created one layer out. That is P1-73's shape exactly: a schema default that became a supplied argument because the receiver merged it. It was MEASURED that the client in use today does not materialise defaults; that is a property of that client, not of the contract.

SCOPE IS BOUNDED AND THE BOUNDARY IS TESTED. 14 tools take an `account`. Only FIVE have an addon handler that refuses without one, and only those five may become required. For a read like nt_orders or nt_fill_events, omitting the account reasonably means "across all accounts"; making those required would break a working call and fix nothing. There is a PASSING test asserting seven of them stay optional. Do not touch it, and do not make it fail.

tickets.title: P1-91: four tool schemas still advertise `default: 'Sim101'` for an account the addon now refuses -- delete the defaults and declare the account required on the five tools whose handler refuses without it
tickets.defect:
`lib/tools.js` declares `default: 'Sim101'` on the `account` property of four tools -- `nt_place_oco_order`, `nt_place_atm_order`, `nt_compliance_report` and `nt_deploy_strategy`. TWO OF THEM PLACE ORDERS. Since P1-90 the NT8 addon refuses a missing or unresolvable account rather than substituting one, so (a) the contract now misdescribes the addon, telling callers that omitting `account` targets Sim101, and (b) any MCP client that materialises schema defaults would inject `Sim101` into an order call, at which point the addon resolves a name the caller never sent and the refusal is never reached.

Separately, none of the five tools whose handler refuses a missing account declares `account` in its `required` array -- including `nt_place_order`, which carries no default and so was not among the four originally filed. A field the handler cannot proceed without, left out of `required`, fails late and further from its cause.
tickets.spec:
In `lib/tools.js`:

1. DELETE the `default: 'Sim101'` from the `account` property of `nt_place_oco_order`, `nt_place_atm_order`, `nt_compliance_report` and `nt_deploy_strategy`. Keep the `type` and the `description`. Do not add a replacement default of any kind.

2. Add `'account'` to the `required` array of these five tools: `nt_place_order`, `nt_place_oco_order`, `nt_place_atm_order`, `nt_compliance_report`, `nt_deploy_strategy`.
   - APPEND to the existing array; do not rewrite it. Losing `idempotencyKey` from an order tool would admit duplicate orders, which is worse than the defect being fixed, and a test pins those entries.
   - `nt_compliance_report` has NO `required` array today. Add one containing exactly `['account']`.

3. Change NOTHING else. Do not touch the other nine tools that take an `account`. Do not add a `default:` to any field. Do not rename a tool or a property -- an MCP tool name is a published contract. Preserve the aligned-property formatting inside `inputSchema.properties`.
tickets.context:
`lib/tools.js` is pure data: one exported `const TOOLS = [...]` of 52 tool descriptors, extracted from nt-mcp-server.js so that tests can import the real schema objects instead of grepping source text. Importing the server itself starts its stdin readline loop and hangs, which is why `lib/copier-config-request.js` was split out before this and says so in its own header.

ESM, not CommonJS: `package.json` sets `"type": "module"`. Zero dependencies, Node builtins only.

The five tools and their handlers in nt8-mcp-bridge, all of which now refuse:
  nt_place_order        -> PlaceOrder
  nt_place_oco_order    -> PlaceOcoOrder
  nt_place_atm_order    -> PlaceAtmOrder
  nt_compliance_report  -> GetComplianceReport
  nt_deploy_strategy    -> DeployStrategy

One acceptance test is deliberately WIDER than the four filed instances: no tool may carry a default on `account`, `action`, `quantity`, `price`, `limitPrice` or `stopPrice`. That is the defect class rather than its four instances, and pinning the rest of it is cheap now. If a default on one of those fields exists elsewhere in the file, it is in scope.

nor a default for any other field
